orientation.central_question: How does a system use feedback to regulate its behavior?
orientation.one_sentence_answer: A feedback system compares observed behavior with a target and uses the difference to adjust its next action.
takeaways: Feedback closes the loop between an action and its observed effect.
The sign and timing of the response determine whether behavior stabilizes or amplifies.
Useful control requires a measurable target, an observation, and an adjustment rule.

groups.title: Foundations

groups.summary: How comparison and adjustment change system behavior.

groups.title: Application and limits
groups.summary: How to apply the loop and recognize failure conditions.

concepts.title: Target state
concepts.statement: The target states the behavior the system is trying to maintain or reach.
details: It must be defined in a measurable form.
concepts.recall_cue: What value is the loop trying to protect?

concepts.title: Observation
concepts.statement: The observation measures the system's current behavior so it can be compared with the target.
details: Measurement delay and noise affect the comparison.
concepts.recall_cue: What does the controller actually know?

concepts.title: Error signal
concepts.statement: The difference between target and observation becomes the signal that drives correction.
details: Its sign determines the direction of adjustment.
concepts.recall_cue: Which difference causes the next action?

concepts.title: Adjustment
concepts.statement: The controller converts the error signal into an action that changes the system state.
details: Gain determines how strongly the controller responds.

concepts.title: Stable regulation
concepts.statement: A well-tuned negative-feedback loop reduces deviations and settles near the target.
concepts.recall_cue: What behavior shows that regulation works?

concepts.title: Delay as a boundary
concepts.statement: Long delay can make a correction arrive after conditions have changed, causing oscillation or instability.
details: More aggressive adjustment can worsen delayed feedback.
concepts.recall_cue: When can a corrective loop amplify error?

relations.label: sets the comparison baseline
relations.why: An error cannot be calculated without a desired value.

relations.label: supplies the measured state
relations.why: The current observation is the second input to the comparison.

relations.label: drives the corrective action
relations.why: The controller uses the error signal to determine its response.

relations.label: reduces deviation when tuned
relations.why: Appropriate corrective action moves the system toward the target.

relations.label: can turn correction into oscillation
relations.why: Delayed responses may act on an outdated system state.

logic_chain: Calculate the difference between target and observation.
Apply a correction and observe its next effect.

distinctions.rule: Negative feedback opposes deviation; positive feedback reinforces the direction of change.

recall_prompts: Name the minimum components of a closed feedback loop.
Explain why delay can destabilize an otherwise corrective loop.
Predict what happens when adjustment gain is too high.
